prize_parts.citation: for the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules bring a chosen protein and an E3 ubiquitin ligase together, from PROTACs to the cereblon mechanism of molecular glues

statement.case_for: After reading all eight first-round statements I move to a single prize part, targeted protein degradation (B027), with Crews, Deshaies and Handa. The mechanism is a defined chemical event: a small molecule enforces proximity between a target and an E3 ligase, the target is ubiquitinated and the proteasome removes it. That event has been shown in vitro, in cells and structurally, and has been reproduced by many independent groups, which is the test I apply. Handa's identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target turned an old drug into a measurable molecular mechanism and explains the whole glue class. Crews and Deshaies conceived and first demonstrated the PROTAC. A three-name citation therefore covers both founding branches without a fourth person. This is a cleaner answer to the chair's question than my two-part pairing, whose second part (Liu alone) added a different field mainly to fit the three-person limit.
statement.case_against: No degrader is, to my knowledge, approved as a drug, and I am working from memory on clinical status. Credit is crowded: Ciulli (VHL ligands, ternary-complex structure), Sakamoto, Ito, Kim and Gray have real claims and are left out. A single citation may merge two discoveries made by different groups at different times, the PROTAC concept (2001) and cereblon as the glue target (2010). Selectivity, resistance and off-target degradation are still being quantified, and a committee that wants a longer clinical record could reasonably wait. Base editing (B038) remains the more conservative fallback with the cleanest single-person attribution, and ionizable lipid nanoparticles (B062) have the strongest proven patient impact.

responses.point: Linke, as chair, moved his third name from Ciulli to Handa and asks whether a single citation conflates the PROTAC and cereblon glue discoveries.
responses.response: I now agree with the Crews, Deshaies and Handa trio and withdraw my Crews/Handa-only version. The two branches share one chemical principle, induced proximity to an E3 ligase, and the cereblon result is what explains the glue branch in molecular terms, so one citation can honestly name both if it states the principle and not a single modality. I accept your point that Ciulli is the most notable omission. His VHL ligand and ternary-complex work refines a concept that Crews and Deshaies had already shown, so I do not regard him as indispensable to the founding discovery.

responses.point: Brzezinski argues degraders are a less awkward fit than base editing because no earlier prize covers the modality, and that base editing should wait for a later year.
responses.response: I accept this and it is part of why I give up the B038 pairing. The 2020 CRISPR prize makes the committee decide whether base editing is a new chemical principle or an application of a recognised platform. I think it is a real chemical principle, but the conceptual step of fusing an impaired Cas9 to an existing deaminase makes it a harder first-year case than degraders. I also take your point that the reports should state explicitly whether the glue branch belongs in the same citation. I would want them to say that the cereblon mechanism explains thalidomide-type molecular glues.

responses.point: Aqvist ranks B027 first with Crews, Deshaies and Handa, accepts that no degrader is approved, and calls the allocation a close, contestable judgement.
responses.response: I now share your trio and the reasoning. On maturity, I think the criterion is confirmation of the mechanism, not an approved drug, and here the mechanism is independently confirmed in vitro, in cells and structurally. I would not claim more for clinical status than I can check. I also agree that base editing with Liu alone is a strong fallback if the degradation allocation cannot be settled, which is why B038 stays as my first alternative, but I do not think it is more mature than degraders.

responses.point: Aili prefers ionizable lipid nanoparticles (B062), now with Cullis, Madden and Hope, and concedes the trio omits later optimisation and siRNA translation.
responses.response: Your argument that the pKa-tuned design is chemistry is stronger after Sparr's phase-behaviour point, and I accept that the 2023 Medicine prize concerns the mRNA cargo and not the carrier. My difficulty is still attribution. When Aili, Sparr and Zou give three different trios from six credited names, I cannot defend any cut. I also still lack evidence on what controls endosomal release beyond lipid pKa. I keep B062 as an alternative, and I would support it later if the committee can state which discovery the citation honours.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts one citation spanning PROTACs and cereblon molecular glues, or sees two discoveries.
Whether Ciulli or Sakamoto should replace a named laureate; I cannot resolve this from the statements alone.
Whether the absence of an approved degrader makes the prize premature; my clinical statements are from memory and unverified.
Degrader selectivity, resistance and off-target effects are still being quantified.
Whether my biology-class background leads me to overweight biochemical mechanism relative to chemical novelty.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile. My work on nucleotide metabolism and DNA replication fidelity is adjacent to ubiquitin-dependent protein turnover and DNA editing, but I have no direct collaboration with any credited candidate. As a biology-class member, my view of B027 and B038 is shaped by that background. Because I no longer put B038 in my preferred configuration, that adjacency now bears on my alternative only.
